Si quis in quadragesima sanctum uelum in populo sine recto deponat, emendet C uiginti sol.

Wenn jemand zu Fasten Kirchenrecht öffentlich ohne Dispens bei Seite setzt, büsse er mit 120 Schill.
If someone in Lent publicly sets aside church law without dispensation, let him pay 120 shillings.
If anyone, without permission, publicly disregards the laws of the Church during Lent, he shall pay 120 shillings compensation.
If anyone openly neglects the rules of the Church in Lent without permission, he is to pay 120 shillings compensation.
If someone in the folk sets aside holy law without dispensation during Lent, let him compensate with 120 shillings

Vgl. Gl Fasten 3. 5. a. 10. Halig heisst ‘geistlich, kirchlich’ in Verbindung mit had (Klerus), hrægl, rift; halig bebodu (Guthlac 5), gastlic-, Godes riht, þeaw arwurðra rihta (Toller 796), z. T. im Ggs. zu profanem Recht, bedeutet ‘kanonisches Recht’. Alecgan heisst ‘discontinue a practice [des Predigens; Toller Suppl. 11a]’, riht alecgan ‘Recht beugen’ V As 1, 3. Af suspendiert nur das zu anderen Zeiten Unverbotene, soweit es kirchlichem Fastengebot widerstreitet, also Fleischgenuss, Rechtsgeschäft, gerechte Rache, Eheschliessung (? s. Gl 13a), nicht aber Missetat, die nie erlaubt sein konnte. — Dagegen ‘heiligen Vorhang’ (s. d. Gl) verstehen der Abschreiber Ld und der Übersetzer Q. Zwar ist für haligrift nur die Bed. ‘Schleier der Nonne oder Witwe’ belegt (Toller), doch rift allein kann ‘velamen, palla, Tempelvorhang’ heissen. Die Altarverhüllung in Fasten (s. Gl 4), das velum quadragesimale (Ducange s. v.) ist für England bezeugt [bei Chambers Divine worship (13. Jh.), Fowler Memorials of Ripon III p. xxxiij, in Sarum charters ed. Jones 369, Use of Sarum ed. Frere I 139] und schon für Agsächs. Zeit bei Ælfric aus Æthelwold’s Concordia regul. ed. Kitchin Compotus rolls of Winchester 182. Durch das Vorhergehen des Eindringens in Häuser mochten die Gedanken der Schreiber auf das Eindringen in den Chor der Kirche verfallen. Allein einen Zweck der Vorhangbeseitigung erkenn ich nicht. Dazu kommt, dass sie nicht etwas ist, was — wie laut butan leafe für das von Af Gemeinte notwendig — ausnahmsweise erlaubt werden kann. — Als Strafe fordert Af ‘Ungehorsam’ (s. d. Gl 7), nur ‘Strafgeld bzw. Rechtsbruchbusse’ spät. Recht

Cf. Gl Fasten 3. 5. a. 10. Halig means ‘spiritual, ecclesiastical’ in combination with had (clergy), hrægl, rift; halig bebodu (Guthlac 5), gastlic-, Godes riht, þeaw arwurðra rihta (Toller 796), partly in contrast to secular law, means ‘canon law’. Alecgan means ‘discontinue a practice [of preaching; Toller Suppl. 11a]’, riht alecgan ‘pervert justice’ V As 1, 3. Af suspends only what is not forbidden at other times, in so far as it conflicts with the Church’s command to fast, i.e. eating meat, legal transactions, lawful vengeance, marriage (? see Gl 13a), but not wrongdoing, which could never have been permitted. — On the other hand, the copyist Ld and the translator Q understand ‘holy curtain’ (see that word in Gl). It is true that for haligrift only the meaning ‘veil of a nun or widow’ is attested (Toller), but rift by itself can mean ‘velamen, palla, temple curtain’. The veiling of the altar in Lent (see Gl 4), the velum quadragesimale (Ducange s. v.), is attested for England [in Chambers Divine worship (13th cent.), Fowler Memorials of Ripon III p. xxxiij, in Sarum charters ed. Jones 369, Use of Sarum ed. Frere I 139], and already for the Anglo-Saxon period in Ælfric, from Æthelwold’s Concordia regul. ed. Kitchin Compotus rolls of Winchester 182. The preceding mention of forcible entry into houses may have turned the scribes’ thoughts to forcible entry into the choir of the church. But I can see no purpose in removing the curtain. Moreover, it is not something that — as must be the case for what Af meant, according to butan leafe — could be permitted by way of exception. — As the penalty Af demands ‘disobedience’ (see that word in Gl 7); only later law demands ‘fine or compensation for breach of law’
openlice Fasten brechen qualifiziert die Missetat auch II Cn 46. — folc bedeutet ‘Öffentlichkeit’ auch in den Compositis folcleasung, folcefiren, folcgestreon
Breaking the fast openlice also aggravates the offence in II Cn 46. — folc also means ‘the public’ in the compounds folcleasung, folcefiren, folcgestreon
‘Bischofs Erlaubnis’ heisst die Befreiung von einem Kanon; Af 8 und Agsä. Beda IV 5 ed Miller 278. — Zu frei ‘Berechtigung’ Q
‘Bishop’s permission’ is the term for dispensation from a canon; Af 8 and A.-S. Beda IV 5 ed Miller 278. — ‘Entitlement’ Q, too free

Quadr. has sanctum velum which is evidently based on the same reading as Ld (halig rift) and refers probably to the hangings of the altar; but, as Liebermann remarks, this would not have been permitted, even exceptionally.
